newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan April c/a surplus seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan April c/a surplus seen rising.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is expected to rise substantially in April from the year earlier period, due to a drop in imports from sluggish domestic demand after the increase in the consumption tax, economists said on Friday.
The data is to be announced at 8.50 a.m. on June 11, Wednesday (2350 GMT, June 10, Tuesday).

A Reuters poll of economists showed, on average, that the April current account surplus would grow to 1.13 trillion yen, compared with a surplus of 566.6 billion yen last year. The forecasts ranged from 990 billion yen to 1.21 trillion yen.

"The main reason for the increase is the jump in the customs-cleared trade surplus for April, which grew over 160 percent. After imports grew in March from the rush in demand before the consumption tax increase, they dropped in April. At the same time, exports continued to grow," said Shuji Shirota, an economist at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc.
Japan raised its consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Economists also pointed out that the rise in April would be especially noticeable since the figure last year was small.
Matthew Poggi, an economist at Lehman Brothers Japan, said there was the possibility that the services trade may be in surplus as well.

"The rise in the consumption tax will have depressed demand, and especially overseas travel will probably fall so that is is a much smaller deficit than usual. That would be enough to tip it over into a surplus," he said.

A decline in individual investors' foreign bond purchases and recent foreign investors' buying of Japanese stocks have worked to cap rises in income from overseas investments, Nomura Research Institute economist Kyohei Morita said.
Yamaichi's Shirota said the current account surplus will continue to rise in the first half of the fiscal year started in April, with growth of 20 to 30 percent expected in May and June.

Nomura's Morita said the surplus will continue to grow, helped by strong exports to the United States in the first half of the fiscal year. But in the latter half, an expected slowdown in the U.S. economy and a stronger yen will cap growth, he said.

Daiwa Bank Research said it sees little possibility the current account surplus will expand drastically, taking into account the recent strength of the yen. Rather, the growth in the surplus from a year ago is likely to stay in 10 to 20 percent range.
The following are forecasts given for April unadjusted current account data:
Yamaichi Research Institute 1.10 trln yen
IBJ 1.21 trln yen
Daiwa Bank Research 1.1985 trln yen
NCB Research Institute 1.15 trln yen
Salomon Brothers 1.20 trln yen
Merrill Lynch 990 bln yen
Lehman Brothers 1.152 trln yen
Nomura Research Institute 1.0239 trln yen
